socketasynceventargs-pooling-ownership.title: Pool SocketAsyncEventArgs with strict operation ownership
socketasynceventargs-pooling-ownership.short: Reuse socket operation state without overlapping use
socketasynceventargs-pooling-ownership.summary: SocketAsyncEventArgs can be pooled to reduce allocations in high-throughput socket servers, but each instance represents mutable operation state.
socketasynceventargs-pooling-ownership.why: Reusing one instance concurrently or returning it before completion can mix buffers, endpoints, and completion state across operations.
socketasynceventargs-pooling-ownership.tips: Give each in-flight operation exclusive ownership, reset mutable fields before reuse, and return the instance only after completion.

conditionalweaktable-metadata-lifetime.title: Attach metadata without extending key lifetime with ConditionalWeakTable
conditionalweaktable-metadata-lifetime.short: Associate auxiliary state with objects while allowing their collection
conditionalweaktable-metadata-lifetime.summary: ConditionalWeakTable stores values associated with object keys without making key reachability behave like a normal strong dictionary key.
conditionalweaktable-metadata-lifetime.why: A normal long-lived dictionary used for per-object metadata can accidentally keep otherwise unreachable objects alive.
conditionalweaktable-metadata-lifetime.tips: Use it for identity-based auxiliary metadata, not as a general-purpose weak cache with deterministic enumeration or eviction requirements.

assemblyloadcontext-collectible-unload-r.title: Release roots before unloading collectible AssemblyLoadContext
assemblyloadcontext-collectible-unload-r.short: Unload begins only after references into the plugin context disappear
assemblyloadcontext-collectible-unload-r.summary: A collectible AssemblyLoadContext can unload plugin assemblies, but live objects, Types, delegates, threads, or other roots can keep the context reachable.
assemblyloadcontext-collectible-unload-r.why: Calling Unload is cooperative and does not invalidate references that application code still retains.
assemblyloadcontext-collectible-unload-r.tips: Stop plugin work, detach callbacks, clear caches and references, call Unload, and use weak references when diagnosing contexts that remain alive.

ratelimiter-lease-disposal-permit-return.title: Dispose RateLimiter leases after protected work
ratelimiter-lease-disposal-permit-return.short: A successful lease may own resources or permits that need release
ratelimiter-lease-disposal-permit-return.summary: RateLimiter acquisition returns a lease describing whether access was granted and carrying the lifetime of the acquired permission.
ratelimiter-lease-disposal-permit-return.why: Ignoring lease disposal can delay release semantics for limiter implementations that associate resources with a lease.
ratelimiter-lease-disposal-permit-return.tips: Use using or await using as appropriate around the protected operation and inspect failed lease metadata when retry guidance matters.

sequencereader-segmented-protocol-parsin.title: Parse segmented buffers with SequenceReader
sequencereader-segmented-protocol-parsin.short: Read protocol fields without assuming one contiguous memory block
sequencereader-segmented-protocol-parsin.summary: SequenceReader helps parse ReadOnlySequence data across segment boundaries while tracking a logical reader position.
sequencereader-segmented-protocol-parsin.why: Code that assumes delimiters or fixed fields live in one Span can fail when pipelines split the same message across segments.
sequencereader-segmented-protocol-parsin.tips: Treat incomplete fields as normal, advance only after successful parsing, and preserve unconsumed data for the next read.

eventcounter-observability-cost-boundary.title: Keep runtime counters cheap enough for hot paths
eventcounter-observability-cost-boundary.short: Observability should not dominate the operation being measured
eventcounter-observability-cost-boundary.summary: Event counters can expose rates and measurements to diagnostics tooling with relatively low overhead when updates remain simple.
eventcounter-observability-cost-boundary.why: Heavy formatting, allocation, or high-cardinality work around every counter update can turn diagnostics into a performance problem.
eventcounter-observability-cost-boundary.tips: Record compact numeric signals in hot paths and move expensive aggregation or interpretation to consumers where possible.

memorycache-size-limit-units.title: Define consistent units for MemoryCache size limits
memorycache-size-limit-units.short: SizeLimit does not automatically measure object memory
memorycache-size-limit-units.summary: MemoryCache size limits depend on application-defined entry sizes, so every producer sharing a limited cache must use the same unit convention.
memorycache-size-limit-units.why: Mixing bytes, item counts, and arbitrary weights makes eviction behavior meaningless and entries without sizes may be rejected in a size-limited cache.
memorycache-size-limit-units.tips: Document one unit, assign a size to every entry, and keep dedicated limited caches separate when unrelated components cannot share a sensible scale.

unsafeaccessor-private-member-versioning.title: Treat UnsafeAccessor as a version-sensitive private contract
unsafeaccessor-private-member-versioning.short: Direct private-member access trades reflection overhead for tighter coupling
unsafeaccessor-private-member-versioning.summary: UnsafeAccessor can bind code to otherwise inaccessible members without ordinary reflection invocation, but those members remain implementation details.
unsafeaccessor-private-member-versioning.why: Renaming or changing a private member can break the accessor even when no public API compatibility promise was violated.
unsafeaccessor-private-member-versioning.tips: Keep usage narrow, cover the binding with tests, and prefer public APIs when compatibility across runtime or library versions matters.

jsonextensiondata-forward-compatible-fie.title: Preserve unknown JSON fields with JsonExtensionData when forwarding data
jsonextensiondata-forward-compatible-fie.short: Capture properties outside the current model instead of discarding them
jsonextensiondata-forward-compatible-fie.summary: JsonExtensionData stores otherwise unmatched JSON properties so a model can retain data introduced by newer producers.
jsonextensiondata-forward-compatible-fie.why: A read-modify-write service can silently delete fields it does not understand if unknown properties are discarded during deserialization.
jsonextensiondata-forward-compatible-fie.tips: Use extension data only when preservation is part of the compatibility contract and define how collisions with known properties are handled.

httpclientfactory-handler-lifetime-dns.title: Choose IHttpClientFactory handler lifetime with connection reuse and DNS in mind
httpclientfactory-handler-lifetime-dns.short: Client reuse and handler rotation solve different lifetime problems
httpclientfactory-handler-lifetime-dns.summary: IHttpClientFactory reuses underlying handlers for configured periods while creating lightweight HttpClient instances for consumers.
httpclientfactory-handler-lifetime-dns.why: Treating every HttpClient creation as a new connection pool or rotating handlers too aggressively can undermine connection reuse without improving name resolution behavior.
httpclientfactory-handler-lifetime-dns.tips: Keep client creation cheap through the factory, choose handler lifetime deliberately for the deployment environment, and measure connection churn before tuning it.
